item.title: 2026 G League draft results: Who did OKC Blue add to roster?
item.description: The 2026 G League draft has come and gone. The OKC Blue added three players to their roster ahead of the 2026-27 regular season. The two-round process happened throughout Saturday, Oct. 24. The G League had all 31 teams participate in its annual draft. It involved the 30 NBA G League affiliates plus the Mexico City Capitanes. The Oklahoma City Thunder were part of it. Even though there were 62 player slots, teams could pass on selections. The G League draft allows teams to sign the rights to free-agent players who aren't part of an NBA parent franchise. The pool of players includes undrafted rookies, international players and former NBA guys trying to make it back into the league. The Texas Legends selected Jeremy Sochan with the No. 1 pick of the 2026 G League draft. The Blue added three players from this year's class. Let's take a quick look at them: No. 5: Jailen Bedford, Virginia Tech The Blue added Bedford with the No. 5 pick of Round 1. He played in three collegiate seasons from 2023-26. He first played at Oral Roberts and then at UNLV and finally for Virginia Tech. He averaged 12.0 points on 40.4% shooting, 4.6 rebounds and 1.1 assists in his collegiate career. No. 9: Yusuf Mohamed, Westminster (UT) The Blue added Mohamed with the No. 9 pick of Round 1. He played one collegiate season at the D-I level at Tennessee State in the 2020-21 season. He averaged 5.6 points on 33.7% shooting, 4.4 rebounds and 0.4 assists. Since then, he's hopped around the semi-pro scenes. No. 36: Trey Galloway, Indiana The Blue added Galloway with the No. 36 pick of Round 2. He played in five collegiate seasons from 2020-25. All at Indiana. He averaged 7.3 points on 44.9% shooting, 2.4 rebounds and 3.1 assists in his collegiate career. item.description: Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images Lee Westwood has been involved in plenty of controversy during his time with LIV Golf, often arguing with fans online about the merits of players joining the league in the first place. However, the 53-year-old has undoubtedly regressed as a golfer since his move to LIV Golf. Lee Westwood is obviously not the player he once was, but that is understandable at his age. However, he has remained in the news more than most LIV Golf players due to his online presence and constant arguments with anyone who dared to question the merits of the league. Now Westwood has received even more criticism after a statement that he made in response to suggestions that LIV golfers should be refused a straightforward DP World Tour return. item.title: “It’s a fantastic goal” Ray Parlour really enjoyed that Gabriel goal
item.description: “It’s a fantastic goal” Ray Parlour really enjoyed that Gabriel goal Gabriel scored again for Arsenal as his goal helped the Gunners secure an important 2-0 victory against Everton this afternoon , earning praise from former midfielder Ray Parlour. The Brazilian defender has regularly contributed goals for Arsenal and scored several important ones last season. His ability to threaten opponents in the penalty area has made him a valuable asset to Mikel Arteta, who continues to rely on him at both ends of the pitch. Gabriel’s consistency explains why he remains one of the first names on the team sheet at the Emirates. His defensive strength and attacking contributions have made him an important figure as Arsenal pursue their ambitions this season. Gabriel strengthens Arsenal’s defence With William Saliba still injured, Gabriel has helped Ezri Konsa settle into the team and build an understanding alongside him. Their partnership has provided stability at the back, allowing Arsenal to maintain their defensive standards despite Saliba’s absence. The Frenchman could face a challenge when he returns, given the form Gabriel and Konsa have shown together. However, Gabriel’s position appears secure because of his consistent performances and ability to make a difference in both penalty areas. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) Parlour praises Gabriel’s goal Parlour watched the match and was pleased to see Gabriel find the back of the net. Speaking via Premier League Productions , he praised the delivery from Ben White and the defender’s excellent finish. “It’s a fantastic goal. A great ball into Ben white who hangs it up, Havertz looks like he’s about to get on the end of it but it’s Gabriel behind him with a brilliant header.” The goal highlighted Gabriel’s aerial ability and awareness inside the penalty area. His timing allowed him to take advantage of White’s delivery and finish with a powerful header. For Arsenal, having a defender who can consistently contribute goals is a significant advantage. Gabriel continues to demonstrate his importance to Arteta’s side, and his latest strike helped the Gunners claim another valuable victory. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: European football: Roma snatch late draw in 3-3 thriller as Como win again
item.description: McTominay scores twice for Napoli against Roma Dortmund top Bundesliga after Eintracht Frankfurt win Roma missed the chance to move top of Serie A, but preserved their unbeaten status as Leonardo Balerdi’s 89th-minute goal snatched a thrilling 3-3 draw at Napoli . Scott McTominay put Napoli ahead with his second goal in the 83rd minute, but Balerdi completed his own double to ensure Roma extended their undefeated start to the league campaign to eight matches. Como backed up their Champions League victory over Manchester United as Anastasios Douvikas scored twice in 11 minutes for a 2-0 win against Sassuolo . They climbed to fourth in the table, two points adrift of Inter who host Fiorentina on Sunday. Later on Saturday, Lazio host Parma . Continue reading...

item.title: Leeds United Consider Contract Extension For Their Main Man: Can His System Deliver Europe?
item.description: Leeds United Consider Contract Extension For Their Main Man: Can His System Deliver Europe? Leeds United have made encouraging progress since returning to the Premier League, and Daniel Farke has given the club a clear structure during a demanding period of change. After winning the Championship in 2024/25 and securing a 14th-place finish in their first season back in the top flight, the German has strengthened his position at Elland Road. Seven league matches into the 2026/27 campaign, Leeds have collected 10 points from two wins, four draws and one defeat. Their record reflects a team that can compete with established Premier League sides, although four draws show that Farke still needs greater consistency in turning competitive performances into victories. That progress has encouraged the hierarchy to consider a longer commitment to the manager. According to an exclusive report by Football Insider, Farke has reached an agreement in principle on a new contract that would keep him at Leeds until 2029. Leeds consider extending Farke’s long-term commitment Speaking on Football Insider’s Inside Track podcast, former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness suggested that the 49ers ownership group could extend Farke’s deal again over the next 12 months if he meets the club’s performance targets. The reported agreement would provide continuity while Leeds pursue their ambitions on the pitch and prepare for developments at Elland Road. A stadium redevelopment could strengthen the club’s long-term commercial position, but the board must ensure that spending on infrastructure does not weaken the squad’s ability to compete. Farke has already benefited from substantial backing. Leeds reportedly spent more than £40 million on goalkeeper James Trafford, while centre-back Tarik Muharemovic arrived for a reported £34.1 million. Those investments show the owners’ willingness to support the manager, although transfer fees alone cannot guarantee progress. Nmecha’s future creates another decision for Leeds Away from the contract discussions, Lukas Nmecha faces uncertainty over his own future. Football Insider reports that the striker would consider a pre-contract agreement with a Bundesliga club, with FC Köln among the sides showing interest ahead of January. The German forward’s Leeds contract expires next summer, but the club reportedly won’t sanction a mid-season departure unless they secure a suitable replacement. Dominic Calvert-Lewin remains Farke’s main centre-forward, so losing his understudy without strengthening the attack would leave the manager short of options. item.title: Ami Nakai rallies to win Grand Prix France
item.description: Ami Nakai rallied for the title at Grand Prix France, one year after winning the season-opening event in her breakout competition en route to earning an Olympic bronze medal in Milan. Nakai, an 18-year-old from Japan, jumped from third after Friday's short program with the top free skate Saturday — 149.08 points, matching her personal best skate from France in 2025. She totaled 219.74 points to prevail by 16.92 over Anastasiia Gubanova of Georgia. Italian Lara Naki Gutmann took third. Nakai landed a triple Axel on Saturday after popping the jump in the short. She is the top returning skater from the Olympics with gold medalist Alysa Liu taking the year off and silver medalist Kaori Sakamoto retired. GRAND PRIX FRANCE: Full Results | Broadcast Schedule Japan's Yuna Aoki, who led after Friday's short, dropped to fourth overall with a fifth-place free skate that included a fall. Grand Prix France concludes Sunday with the men's and pairs' free skates, live on Peacock . Earlier Saturday, Olympic gold medalists Laurence Fournier Beaudry and Guillaume Cizeron pulled away to win the ice dance with 207.57 points, distancing Diana Davis and Gleb Smolkin of Georgia by 13.64 points. Americans Christina Carreira and Anthony Ponomarenko returned to the Grand Prix podium in third, after placing fourth and fifth in their two Grand Prix starts last fall. France's Adam Siao Him Fa topped the men's short program with a 102.46-point skate that included a quad toe-triple toe combination and a quad Salchow. Siao Him Fa, who was third, fourth and fifth at the last three World Championships, is trying to win his home Grand Prix for a fourth time. Olympic gold medalist Mikhail Shaidorov from Kazakhstan sits fourth after falling on his opening quad Lutz, putting his hand down on a triple Axel and not having a combination jump. In pairs, Olympic and world silver medalists Anastasiia Metelkina and Luka Berulava of Georgia outscored neutral skaters Aleksandra Boikova and Dmitriy Kozlovskiy from Russia by 1.49 points. Boikova and Kozlovskiy are competing on the top international level for the first time since they placed fourth at the 2022 Olympics. Before this season, the International Skating Union announced that skaters from Russia and Belarus can return to the Grand Prix for the first time since the war in Ukraine started, with neutral status, if they do not support the war. Last season, one men's and one women's singles skater each from Belarus and Russia were allowed to compete in an Olympic qualifier, with three of the four qualifying to compete in the Milan Cortina Games as neutral skaters. Figure skating rules continue to be moving target headed into 2026-27 Grand Prix season The figure skating season moves into full glide this weekend in Angers, France, with the first of seven senior Grand Prix events. Philip Hersh ,

item.title: Beier late show sends Dortmund top of Bundesliga
item.description: Werder Bremen's Niclas Fuellkrug has scored in six straight Bundesliga games. (Kirill KUDRYAVTSEV) Maximilian Beier scored in the 80th minute to send Borussia Dortmund top of the Bundesliga after a hard-fought 1-0 home win over Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday. In a game lacking clear chances, Jobe Bellingham came off the bench and had an instant impact, threading a clever pass for fellow substitute Beier to score. The narrow victory was Dortmund's first in the league since mid-September and took Niko Kovac's side three points clear atop the table. Bayern Munich can return to the top of the standings with a win at Freiburg on Sunday but will be without coach Vincent Kompany, who is being treated in hospital for a mystery virus after collapsing at training on Friday. "We've got a great team. Those who aren't playing from the start, they're the finishers. They're the ones who close out the match, who decide things," Kovac said. "Maxi struck that shot really well. I'm happy for the lad because he's had a tough time lately." Dortmund had started the season with a run of six straight wins but came into Saturday's game in a mini slump, having won just one of their past four in all competitions. The best opportunity of the first half fell to Serhou Guirassy with 15 minutes gone. The Guinean was one on one with Noah Atubolu but tried a soft chip, which the goalkeeper palmed away. Just after the break, Guirassy headed a Joey Veerman corner against the bar. Beier came on for the ineffective Fabio Silva with 22 minutes remaining. With 10 minutes left, he collected a Bellingham pass and curled in the winner from just inside the box. - Fuellkrug 'shines bright' - Niclas Fuellkrug scored for the sixth straight Bundesliga match as his Werder Bremen side won 3-2 at Mainz. Fuellkrug, who returned to Bremen on loan from English Championship side West Ham in the summer, converted two penalties inside the opening 25 minutes to notch up a second straight Bundesliga brace. Ludovit Reis grabbed Bremen's other goal, while Anthony Caci and Lee Jae-sung scored for the hosts. Fuellkrug now has eight goals this season, half of his total in his final campaign in Bremen in 2022/23, when he won the Bundesliga top-goalscorer award. The Germany striker scored just three goals during an injury-hit 18-month spell at West Ham and just one in a six-month loan at AC Milan. Bremen coach praised his in-form striker, telling reporters: "You can tell that he feels comfortable. "He is our guiding star -- and he's shining brightly right now. He's carrying this team along with him." RB Leipzig rebounded from their 4-1 thumping away at Real Madrid midweek with a comfortable 4-0 home win over promoted Elversberg. Romulo scored a double while Tidiam Gomis, who scored Leipzig's only goal at the Bernabeu, and Christoph Baumgartner also got on the scoresheet as the Saxons climbed to fifth. Without a point away from home, Leipzig have now won their four home games by a collective score of 18-0. Pad

item.title: Happy Birthday Chris Colabello
item.description: DUNEDIN, FL - MARCH 07: Chris Colabello #15 of the Toronto Blue Jays swings at a pitch during the first inning of a spring training game against the Atlanta Braves at Florida Auto Exchange Stadium on March 7, 2016 in Dunedin, Florida. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Today marks Chris Colabello’s 43rd birthday. The Blue Jays claimed Chris Colabello off waivers from the Twins before the 2015 season. During his two years with Minnesota, he posted a .214/.284/.364 line with 13 home runs in 114 games. Understandably, expectations were low for a 31-year-old first baseman/DH who hadn’t hit well enough to earn regular playing time. Chris impressed in spring training. When Michael Saunders suffered a knee injury on a sprinkler head in Dunedin, the team suddenly needed outfield help. Dalton Pompey’s slow start and the Jays’ impatience led to Colabello getting the call-up in early May. Colabello played the outfield with all the elegance of a statue—reminiscent of early Jays experiments with Otto Velez—but he found his swing at the plate. By the end of his first month, he was batting an impressive .368/.417/.568. By late June, it was clear Chris’s bat couldn’t make up for his glove in the outfield, so he shifted to first base and DH. Justin Smoak, also new to the 2015 roster, wasn’t having a strong season, though his power was undeniable—when Smoak homered, it was never a cheap shot. Unfortunately, the GameThreads devolved into endless debates about who should play first. For the first time, I found myself avoiding them. Chris nevertheless had an outstanding season, finishing at .321/.367/.520 with 15 home runs in 101 games. His defense limited his value—he posted a 0.7 bWAR. He shined in the ALDS, hitting .375/.412/.688, but struggled in the ALCS, managing only .217/.250/.391. We wondered if he could replicate his success. His .411 BABIP seemed unsustainable to many of us, but with more walks and fewer strikeouts, there was hope he could still produce solid numbers. We never got to find out. Chris began the 2016 season in a slump, hitting just .069/.156/.225. Then came the news of his positive PED test. With MLB’s improved testing, several players were caught that year, and Chris received an 80-game suspension. He claimed not to know how the substance entered his system and gave an emotional interview to Sportsnet. Personally, I’m skeptical of such claims—but who can say for sure? The slow start may have been because he knew the suspension was coming. In 2017, he played in the minors for Cleveland and Milwaukee, hitting .254/.350/.395. He spent 2018 in Italy and 2019 in the independent leagues. I admire players who love the game enough to keep playing, even in the independents. He also played for Italy in the WBC in 2017 and played in Mexico for a season Chris always seemed likable and was fun to watch (if a bit less so in the outfield). I hope things are going well for him. Happy birthday, Chris. Wishing you all the best.

item.title: Deion Sanders’ Stubborn Recruiting Style Called ‘A Bad Look’ Amid Colorado’s Slide
item.description: Deion Sanders and the Colorado Buffaloes are having a difficult period at the moment. They currently have a 2–4 overall record and are winless with a 0–3 record in Big 12 conference play. Having lost four games in a row, the team seems really hopeless. The results have brought much scrutiny into Sanders, with many criticizing his coaching style. One analyst has also questioned his recruiting stance, and gave him a key piece of advice. Analyst questions Deion Sanders’ recruiting stance The team’s relentless offseason reliance on the transfer portal has failed to yield on-field chemistry so far. The offense is averaging a meager 19.5 points per game and the team also ranks near the bottom of the nation (136th) in penalty yards. Oct 17, 2026; Boulder, Colorado, USA; Colorado Buffaloes head coach Deion Sanders against the game against the Utah Utes at Folsom Field. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images FOX Sports analyst RJ Young has also questioned Sanders’ long-standing refusal to conduct in-home or off-campus recruiting visits. He noted that elite coaches such as Kirby Smart have routinely visited prospects’ homes, while Sanders has not. He said , “When you seem to be losing players because Kirby Smart is willing to walk into somebody’s house and you are not, Nick Saban is willing to walk into somebody’s house, you are not. Back when you were still doing that, quite literally every other major college football coach in the country is willing to come into someone else’s house and say hi, have a meal, and have a really good private conversation. That’s a bad look.” He added that Sanders reasoning for the stance is also wrong, “Now Prime’s reasoning is ‘I don’t think many people want me in their houses,’ ‘I don’t think that they want to be apologizing for how their house looks or having to have these discussions about what he must be used to’ and I said that’s exactly what they want.” Sanders has previously explained why he refuses to conduct home visits. Deion Sanders explains recruiting stance Sanders has consistently defended the policy since taking over at Colorado in December 2022. University records obtained by USA TODAY confirmed he has made zero off-campus recruiting contacts, including no home visits, despite a contractual private-travel budget that went unused. In a 2024 press conference, Sanders explained his decision. He said , “I’m a businessman as well, so I try to save our university money every darn chance I get.” He added, “Going there is just showcasing for me. That’s just blowing money. It’s blowing a bag, don’t make sense. I can’t do things other coaches can do. You know why? I’m Coach Prime. And I didn’t stutter when I said it.” Deion Sanders will now focus on his team’s next game against the Oklahoma State Cowboys. item.title: Thioune and Füllkrug savour "incredibly hard-fought" win in Mainz
item.description: Thioune and Füllkrug savour "incredibly hard-fought" win in Mainz After a thrilling 3-2 victory over Mainz earlier this afternoon , Daniel Thioune took time to special praise for their efforts over 90 minutes. “I wanted us to take the lead today and make the most of our chances," the Bremen head coach said in his post-match interview. "Our positioning was excellent today and we managed to get on the ball in exactly the areas we wanted to. "We found plenty of space in the first 20 minutes, which led to the two penalties. We also had to withstand a lot of pressure, though. “What helped us was that we just kept going. We had a lot of defending to do towards the end, but overall, I thought we were the better team,” he added. Scoring a brace from the penalty spot at the Mewa Arena, Niklas Füllkrug underlined just how difficult it was to keep Mainz at bay. “It was an incredibly hard-fought game and we scored in the right moments. Unfortunately, we also conceded pretty quickly afterwards. "I was particularly annoyed about their second goal because we wouldn't have had such a nervy finish if we'd managed to hold on to our two-goal lead for a few more minutes. "Mainz are an incredibly difficult team to play against. Urs Fischer always sets his teams up with a clear plan, and they've got some really good individual players too. They put crosses in whenever they had half a chance. I was absolutely exhausted because defending so deep really takes it out of you," the striker said.

item.title: James Maddison suffers another heartbreaking injury setback for Tottenham in London derby
item.description: James Maddison has suffered another injury setback in a gut-wrenching blow for the Tottenham midfielder. Maddison, who missed nearly the entirety of last season with an ACL tear, was forced off in Spurs’ London derby with Chelsea on Saturday afternoon. He went down soon after the second half got underway at Stamford Bridge, crouching and looking to the bench before hitting the deck as his team-mates signalled team doctors onto the pitch. Maddison walked off the pitch visibly dejected and was replaced by former Chelsea midfielder Conor Gallagher, who was booed as he entered play. He went straight down the tunnel after being substituted, receiving a pat on the back from opposition manager Xabi Alonso. James Maddison went straight down the tunnel after being replaced (PA) Maddison has had his entire Tottenham career plagued by fitness issues and only made his first start since May 2025 against Coventry , when the midfielder scored and starred in a 3-1 win - the club’s first of the season. He missed 24 games in his debut campaign in north London due to an array of issues before suffering a serious knee injury last term, which ruled him out for eight months. The 29-year-old suffered an early injury scare this season when he was forced off in the damning opening day defeat to Brentford due to a shoulder issue, though this setback wasn’t as bad as initially feared. However, Roberto De Zerbi will now face another nervous wait to learn the extent of Maddison’s latest injury, compiling Tottenham’s woes in the medical department. "I think it's not a very important problem,” De Zerbi said in a post-match press conference. “We need to make the medical check. I hope it is not a big problem because he's a special player for us." Several key players were missing for the trip to Chelsea, with Destiny Udogie missing while Tosin Adarabioyo was unable to recover in time to face his former club. Pedro Porro could only start on the bench. But despite a growing injury crisis, De Zerbi defended Tottenham’s medical team , saying: “It’s football. I am convinced our medical staff this season is high level. “I follow them. I believe in them. I have big confidence because I know how they are working. “I think they are good enough to believe in them. Nothing more. We are suffering a normal situation in football.”

Maddison walked off the pitch visibly dejected and was replaced by former Chelsea midfielder Conor Gallagher, who was booed as he entered play. He went straight down the tunnel after being substituted, receiving a pat on the back from opposition manager Xabi Alonso. James Maddison went straight down the tunnel after being replaced (PA) Maddison has had his entire Tottenham career plagued by fitness issues and only made his first start since May 2025 against Coventry , when the midfielder scored and starred in a 3-1 win - the club’s first of the season. He missed 24 games in his debut campaign in north London due to an array of issues before suffering a serious knee injury last term, which ruled him out for eight months. The 29-year-old suffered an early injury scare this season when he was forced off in the damning opening day defeat to Brentford due to a shoulder issue, though this setback wasn’t as bad as initially feared. However, Roberto De Zerbi will now face another nervous wait to learn the extent of Maddison’s latest injury, compiling Tottenham’s woes in the medical department. "I think it's not a very important problem,” De Zerbi said in a post-match press conference. “We need to make the medical check. I hope it is not a big problem because he's a special player for us." Several key players were missing for the trip to Chelsea, with Destiny Udogie missing while Tosin Adarabioyo was unable to recover in time to face his former club. Pedro Porro could only start on the bench. But despite a growing injury crisis, De Zerbi defended Tottenham’s medical team , saying: “It’s football. I am convinced our medical staff this season is high level. “I follow them. I believe in them. I have big confidence because I know how they are working. “I think they are good enough to believe in them. Nothing more. We are suffering a normal situation in football.”

item.title: UFC 333 results: Alexander Volkov calls for title shot after latest win with decision over Rizvan Kuniev
item.description: ABU DHABI, UNITED ARAB EMIRATES - OCTOBER 24: (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Alexander Volkov wants his shot at gold after his latest win over Rizvan Kuniev at UFC 333 on Saturday. Already near the top of the heavyweight division, Volkov showed off superior striking and a late submission attempt to thwart Kuniev’s attempt at the upset. Volkov ultimately outdueled his fellow heavyweight in all aspects of the fight with the judges giving scores reading 29-28, 30-27 and 30-27 in his favor. Now Volkov likely awaits the outcome of Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit in November with hopes of getting the winner. “Good fight,” Volkov said about his performance. “I have a question for Dana White? I just started my professional career and I have about 20 fights in the UFC. What do I need to do for a title shot?” Kuniev immediately started throwing kicks at his taller opponent but Volkov had no problem firing back with some of his own. Volkov then started tossing out a lead jab and more kicks to keep Kuniev at a distance. That led to some aggression from Kuniev but Volkov weathered the storm and backed him off with some strikes of his own. Volkov was then constantly moving forward trying to chip away at Kuniev throughout the opening round. In the second round, Volkov snapped off a great left jab that stabbed at Kuniev as his fellow Russian kept trying to close the distance. Volkov was able to fend him off and deliver more strikes as they battled for position. While Kuniev started to take more risks, Volkov maintained his stance and just kept popping him with solid strikes on the feet. With five minutes remaining, Volkov stung Kuniev with a calf-kick and then went back up top with more jabs. But Kuniev fired back with a spinning back fist that landed, although Volkov ate the damaging blow without any issue. A late grappling exchange led to Volkov snatching the back and locking on a rear-naked choke with Kuniev defending well. Volkov couldn’t get under the chin so he kept trying for the submission but Kuniev survived to the final horn. Volkov now has three wins in a row and it’s going to be hard to deny him a shot at the belt unless Tom Aspinall makes his comeback. Otherwise, the Russian has seemingly done everything possible to earn that opportunity after Gane vs. Hokit.

The foul not only checked a promising break, but broke a bone in Coluna’s foot. item.title: Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest
item.description: Amid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. Nothing erudite, anyway. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
